answers.explanation: The page waits for the slowest call, so each service's tail becomes the page's typical experience.
Near capacity, queues grow in bursts. The tail feels it first.
Redundancy keeps a fault (one machine dying) from becoming a failure (users losing service).
Load parameters describe the load. Response time describes performance under that load.
Stateless services scale out easily. Watch the database next: it's the stateful part.
Schema evolution and rolling deployments, later in the course, are evolvability in practice.
The median splits requests in half: half are faster and half are at least that slow.
